footer_about_heading: About RegexStudio — Online Regular Expression Tester & Visualizer
footer_about_p1: RegexStudio is a free, browser-based regex tester, debugger and visualizer that helps developers build, understand and optimize regular expressions. Write a pattern and instantly see real-time matches, capture groups, an interactive railroad diagram, an AST tree view, replacement previews and detailed explanations — all running locally in your browser with zero data sent to any server.
footer_about_p2_prefix: Whether you are learning regex syntax, debugging a tricky pattern, or validating emails, URLs, phone numbers, dates, IP addresses or log lines, RegexStudio supports JavaScript (ECMAScript), PCRE and Python flavors with flags such as
footer_built_with_suffix: for developers who love regular expressions.
flavor_target_compatibility_desc: Matching is always tested with the JavaScript engine. Switching the target only changes which features are flagged as incompatible.
engine_notes_javascript: Native browser engine. Full support for all modern JavaScript regex features.
engine_notes_python: Python re module. Lookbehind must be fixed-width; named groups also accept (?P<name>...) syntax.
engine_notes_pcre2: Most feature-rich target. Supports recursion (?R), atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, and \K resets.
engine_notes_java: Java regex engine. Lookbehind must have a bounded width; supports possessive quantifiers and atomic groups.
engine_notes_go: Go uses RE2, which guarantees linear-time matching but does not support lookaround or backreferences.
engine_notes_dotnet: .NET regex engine. Supports variable-length lookbehind, balancing groups, and named captures with (?<name>...) / (?'name'...).
engine_notes_rust: Rust regex crate guarantees linear-time matching. For lookaround/backreferences, use fancy-regex.

compat_python_lookbehind_message: Python `re` requires fixed-width lookbehind. Alternations or quantifiers inside `(?<=...)` / `(?<!...)` are rejected. Use the third-party `regex` module if you need variable-length lookbehind.
compat_java_lookbehind_message: Java requires lookbehind to have a determinable maximum length. Unbounded quantifiers (* or +) inside `(?<=...)` / `(?<!...)` will be rejected.
compat_go_lookahead_message: Go's regexp package (RE2) does not support lookahead assertions (?=...) or (?!...). Consider restructuring your pattern.
compat_go_lookbehind_message: Go's regexp package (RE2) does not support lookbehind assertions (?<=...) or (?<!...). Consider restructuring your pattern.
compat_go_backreference_message: Go's regexp package (RE2) does not support backreferences (\1, \2, etc.). This is by design for guaranteed linear-time matching.
compat_rust_lookahead_message: Rust's regex crate does not support lookahead assertions. Consider using the `fancy-regex` crate instead.
compat_rust_lookbehind_message: Rust's regex crate does not support lookbehind assertions. Consider using the `fancy-regex` crate instead.
compat_rust_backreference_message: Rust's regex crate does not support backreferences. Consider using the `fancy-regex` crate instead.

codegen_op_test_desc: Check if the string matches the pattern
codegen_op_match_desc: Find the first match in the string
codegen_op_matchAll_desc: Find all matches in the string
codegen_op_capture_desc: Extract named and numbered capture groups
codegen_op_split_desc: Split the string by the pattern
debugger_enter_pattern_hint: Enter a pattern and test text to start debugging
debugger_truncated_warning: Execution truncated at 10,000 steps. The pattern may cause excessive backtracking.
explain_empty: Enter a pattern to see its breakdown
explain_quant_brace_min_or_more: Match {min} or more of the preceding token.
explain_quant_brace_min_max: Match between {min} and {max} of the preceding token.
explain_quant_brace_exact: Match exactly {n} of the preceding token.
explain_quant_plus: Match 1 or more of the preceding token.
explain_quant_star: Match 0 or more of the preceding token.
explain_quant_optional: Match 0 or 1 of the preceding token (optional).
explain_quant_lazy_suffix: Lazy: matches as few times as possible.
explain_alternation_desc: Matches the expression before or after the |.
explain_capturing_group_desc: Groups multiple tokens together and creates a capture group for extracting a substring.
explain_noncap_group_desc: Groups multiple tokens together without creating a capture group.
explain_named_group_desc: Captures the matched text and assigns it to the name "{name}".
explain_lookahead_desc: Asserts that what follows the current position matches.
explain_neg_lookahead_desc: Asserts that what follows does NOT match.
explain_neg_lookbehind_desc: Asserts that what precedes does NOT match.
explain_char_set_desc: Match any single character present in the set.
explain_neg_char_set_desc: Match any single character NOT present in the set.
explain_anchor_start_desc: Matches the beginning of the string, or line with multiline flag (m).
explain_anchor_end_desc: Matches the end of the string, or line with multiline flag (m).
explain_escape_s: Matches any whitespace character (space, tab, newline).
explain_dot_desc: Matches any single character except line terminators (unless dotall flag).
explain_backreference_desc: Matches the same text as previously matched by group #{n}.
